assertions.name: e_lambda_eigenvalue_1_on_own_block
assertions.unit: max over (λ ⊢ 3, T' ∈ SYT(λ)) of |e_λ · v_{T'} − 1|
assertions.source: Lagrange interpolation gives the unique projector with eigenvalue 1 on the desired tableau slot.

assertions.name: e_lambda_orthogonality_off_block
assertions.unit: max over (λ ⊢ 3, μ ⊢ 3 with μ ≠ λ, T' ∈ SYT(μ)) of |e_λ · v_{T'} − 0|
assertions.source: Cells of distinct partitions have distinct content multisets in this regime; the Lagrange product vanishes when JM eigenvalues for T' miss the cell set of λ.

assertions.name: completeness_sum_e_lambda_equals_1
assertions.unit: max over T' ∈ ∪_μ SYT(μ) of |Σ_λ e_λ · v_{T'} − 1|
assertions.source: Σ_λ e_λ = 1 in H_n(q) — partition into Wedderburn blocks is complete.

description: I1 probe for prop:explicit-central-idempotent.  Verifies the Lagrange-interpolation formula for the central primitive idempotents e_λ in H_3(q) — with a scope correction surfaced by the probe.  The proposition's literal statement has the inner product range over cells of λ only; with that scope, the off-block projection does NOT vanish (off-block residue ~3.24e+01).  The CORRECTED formula ranges the inner product over the UNION of cell contents across every μ ⊢ n (= {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} for n = 3), and gives the actual central idempotent structure: e_λ on v_{T'} = δ_{λ,μ}, with completeness Σ_λ e_λ = 1, both to ~1e-50 numerical precision.  Surfacing the correction is a paper-level note flagged via the small-moderate-fix-rides-on-active-PR rule.

formula_scope_correction_note.literal_proposition_scope: Inner Lagrange product ranges over cells of λ only.
formula_scope_correction_note.corrected_scope: Inner Lagrange product ranges over the UNION of distinct cell contents across all μ ⊢ n.  For n = 3 this is {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}.
formula_scope_correction_note.interpretation: The proposition's literal formula projects within the JM-eigenvalue lattice of λ but does not automatically vanish on off-block JM eigenvalues drawn from cells of distinct partitions.  The standard literature formula extends the inner product over the full distinct-content set so that the Lagrange factor (J_k - q^{2c(T'(k))}) appears literally when T' ∈ SYT(μ ≠ λ), forcing off-block vanishing.  Recommendation: update the proposition to make the inner-product scope explicit.
